title: Acid-Base Disorders: Thresholds and Compensation Formulas

units.full: Normal arterial blood gas values are pH 7.35 to 7.45, PaCO2 35 to 45 mmHg, and HCO3- 22 to 26 mEq/L. Acidaemia is defined as pH <7.35 and alkalaemia as pH >7.45. Always evaluate the primary disorder first, then check whether compensation matches the expected formula; compensation never fully normalises pH except possibly in mild chronic respiratory alkalosis.

units.full: High anion gap metabolic acidosis (AG >12 mEq/L) includes methanol, uraemia, diabetic ketoacidosis, propylene glycol, isoniazid or iron, lactic acidosis, ethylene glycol, and salicylates. Normal anion gap (hyperchloraemic) metabolic acidosis results from renal tubular acidosis, diarrhoea, or excessive 0.9% saline infusion.

units.full: Do not assume a normal pH excludes an acid-base disorder: a normal pH with abnormal PaCO2 and HCO3- proves a mixed disorder. Do not rapidly overcorrect chronic respiratory acidosis with aggressive mechanical ventilation, because post-hypercapnic metabolic alkalosis can precipitate arrhythmias and seizures.
